decision_question: Did the Carbolic Smoke Ball Company's advertisement constitute a binding offer capable of acceptance by performance?

claims.text: The advertisement constituted a binding unilateral offer.
Mrs. Carlill accepted the offer by performing the conditions (using the smoke ball).
The company's deposit of £1000 at the bank demonstrated intention to be bound.
No notification of acceptance was required beyond performance.

evidence.text: Advertisement: '£100 reward will be paid by the Carbolic Smoke Ball Company to any person who contracts the increasing epidemic influenza, colds, or any disease caused by taking cold, after having used the ball three times daily for two weeks according to the printed directions supplied with each ball. £1000 is deposited with the Alliance Bank, Regent Street, showing our sincerity in the matter.'

source.title: Carbolic Smoke Ball Advertisement (Pall Mall Gazette, Nov 1891)

evidence.text: Mrs. Carlill purchased a smoke ball, used it three times daily for two weeks as directed, and contracted influenza.

source.title: Witness Statement of Mrs. Louisa Carlill

evidence.text: The company deposited £1000 with the Alliance Bank, Regent Street, as stated in the advertisement.
The company argued the advertisement was mere puffery, not a serious offer, and that acceptance required notification.
